text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty triggered: high-rate auth header fragments found in s3://redwood-logs/staging/debug/ — potential leakage of service tokens. Paging #incidents.

lena: oncall ack, I'm waking up the triage squad.

aj: saw the alert, attaching quick grep I ran from cloud shell.
aj: `aws s3 cp s3://redwood-logs/staging/debug/ - | grep -i 'Authorization' | head -n 5`
aj: results show short bearer-like strings in several files, looks like a debug-forwarder accidentally sent sanitized headers but maybe not fully scrubbed.

ethan: can we confirm these are staging service tokens only? any prod account ids?

sec-bot: Automated scan: tokens match pattern for svcacct-ingest-relay (staging). No prod tenant IDs observed in sampled objects. Risk: medium until keys rotated.

lena: tagging legal and SRE. @legal can you standby for potential notification scope?

legal: on it. need: initial timeline, impacted buckets, and whether any external access to that bucket is public.

aj: bucket ACLs look private, access logs show reads only from internal IP ranges. Copying list: `s3:GetObject` calls all from our VPC endpoints, no external IPs.

sre-lead: good catch. plan proposal: 1) immediate rotate svcacct-ingest-relay key pair for staging 2) invalidate any sessions created in last 24h for that service 3) run full scan for leaked patterns in that prefix and quarantined objects 4) prevent further forwarder pushes to that prefix.

ethan: agree. I can rotate the service account keys and push new credentials to staging env. I'll coordinate with @ops-oncall for safe rollout.

ops-oncall: standing by to apply new creds and restart the relay. ETA 10m after rotate.

lena: assign tasks: ethan -> rotate key and post new creds to staging secret (vault). aj -> run quick grep scan across prefix and collect filenames with matches. ops-oncall -> restart relay to pick up new secret. I'll notify legal & customer success if scope expands.

aj: starting scan now. snippet: `aws s3 ls s3://redwood-logs/staging/debug/ --recursive | awk '{print $4}' | xargs -n1 -I {} sh -c "aws s3 cp s3://redwood-logs/staging/debug/{} - | grep -H \"Authorization\" || true"`

incident-bot: ack assigned: incident_id=INC-2026-1982, priority=P2, channel=#incidents.

ethan: rotated keys. New key uploaded to vault path `secret/staging/svcacct-ingest-relay`. Old key disabled.

ops-oncall: restarting relay pods now (k8s rollout).

ops-oncall: relay pods restarted and read new secret. smoke test logs show no outbound debug header forwarding.

aj: scan complete. Found 14 objects with Authorization-like strings; copying list to the incident ticket. No object appears to have prod tenant IDs.

sec-bot: recommended: rotate any long-lived tokens issued by the old key and invalidate sessions where possible. For staging we will revoke tokens associated with svcacct-ingest-relay.

lena: executing session invalidation for staging svcacct. `authctl revoke --service ingest-relay --since 24h`

ethan: revoke command completed. Confirmed 6 active sessions terminated.

legal: based on current data, no customer PII or production tokens observed. We'll keep monitoring and prepare a short internal memo. If anything changes, we'll escalate external notification.

sre-lead: follow-up actions: - Add lifecycle hook to debug-forwarder to drop Authorization headers - Create S3 object lifecycle/quarantine for debug prefix - Add alert to detect header-like patterns with higher sensitivity - Postmortem to include timeline and controls.

lena: who will own postmortem? I can draft and loop in eng-infra and sec.

aj: I'll attach the scan logs and the list of filenames to the ticket.

ops-oncall: everything green from infra side. no customer impact detected, services healthy.

incident-bot: status update: mitigation complete, incident moved to monitoring. Please add notes to INC-2026-1982.

lena: closing the live bridge. we'll keep monitoring for 24h and reconvene if any new indicators surface. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

legal: recorded for compliance. request retention of incident artifacts for 1 year.

sre-lead: +1 on retention. Also schedule a short rollout to production to ensure debug-forwarder guard is in place before any env parity changes.

lena: last check-in: watchlist set, alert thresholds lowered for 48h. closing thread.

ops-oncall: last_message: all clear, unpagable unless new alerts.
